description: §7.6 rule (b) (S482) — `${ const a = note("a"); }` written inside the content of an `if=` element: the initializer calls a function, and a file-scope initializer runs once — not when, or each time, the branch shows — so it has no single place: a value position (§6.15 item 4, S482), and `note` writes the file-scope `log` — E-VALUE-WRITES-STATE, naming the construct.
rationale: §7.6 rule (b) (S482): "A file-scope initializer written there that acts — a call, a write, a `?{}` query, a foreign block — SHALL be a compile error, `E-FILE-SCOPE-INIT-IN-CONSTRUCT`, whose message names the construct." ruling:user-voice-scrml.md-S481-nested-init-chain-comments item 1 — "make it a compile error naming the construct; refusing means nobody is surprised." (owner: "aprove both, lets wrap"). s482 (lane s482-value-no-write): ruling:user-voice-scrml.md-S482-runorder-model-c A1 ("yes, adopt (c) with the riders") — such an initializer has no single place, so it is a value position (§6.15 item 4), and one that writes a file-scope `let` (`note` writes `log`) is E-VALUE-WRITES-STATE; a call of a function that writes nothing is no longer acting (~~E-FILE-SCOPE-INIT-IN-CONSTRUCT~~).
